 Vile UFC star who called Michelle Obama a man says Trump reason made it 'worth it'
 Josh Hokit is happy he made his vile remark about Michelle Obama at the White House, saying he was glad to be featured on President Trump's social media page
 Add to preferred sources Comments Ryan Gerbosi Deputy Sports Editor 12:21 ET, 11 Nov 2026 Updated 12:38 ET, 11 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Josh Hokit continues to show no remorse for his remark about Michelle Obama at the UFC's White House event (Image: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) 
 NEW YORK — Josh Hokit made it clear he has zero regrets about calling Michelle Obama a man during his post-fight speech at UFC Freedom 250 earlier this year, explaining exactly why it was worth disparaging the former first lady on an international stage.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 The mixed martial arts star will be back in action at UFC 334 on Saturday at Madison Square Garden, where he'll face heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane in the main event with the title on the line.
 Hokit became well known beyond the MMA world in June when he took the microphone after defeating Derrick Lewis on the White House South Lawn, calling the wife of former President Barack Obama "a man," much to the chagrin of UFC president Dana White. 
 ‌ 
 READ MORE : Dana White snubs Donald Trump job offer to become White House press secretary READ MORE : UFC star Sean Strickland claims Donald Trump 'failed Americans' on immigration Five months removed from the incident, Hokit does not have an iota of remorse for the remark, saying the reaction and attention it created, including from President Donald Trump on his Truth Social profile, made it all worth it.
 When asked if he regretted the comment during UC 334 media day on Wednesday, Hokit broke into what he claimed was a freestyle rap, then said he does not look in the past.
 "I'll never look back and be like, no, I regret that," Hokit said.
 ‌ 
 When asked if it was the right venue for such comments, Hokit said, "I'm sure it wasn't, but I mean, it is what it is. I made it on Donald Trump's True Social post. You know what I'm saying? Are you on Donald Trump's True Social post? Well, that sucks."
 View 2 Images Josh Hokit made waves well beyond the MMA world with his remark in June
 ‌ 
 "At the end of the day, my name's gonna live on forever, you know what I'm saying? And media people, whatever you do not like it, but It is what it is.
 "I'm here to be remembered, and if I gotta crack a few eggs to make an omelet, f--- it. If I gotta burn the bridge to light the way, f--- it. You know what I'm saying?
 ‌ 
 "So I'm here to take what's mine. And if I gotta rub some people the wrong way, if I gotta say some s--- in the wrong location, it is what it is.
 "Was it not a good location to say it? I mean, we're at the White House. That house represents freedom of speech. So it is what it is. I think that was a perfect location to say it."
 READ MORE : Donald Trump refuses to make UFC 334 prediction to avoid 'getting into trouble' READ MORE : Dana White says Donald Trump would beat Joe Biden in UFC fight after White House offer A former college football star turned fighter, Hokit proved to be the biggest story of the UFC's White House event, knocking out Lewis, who was on the card as Trump's favorite fighter.
 Hokit followed up his win by placing a gold chain around Trump's neck and shaking hands with the president.
 In the months since, he has continued to display the same type of vile behavior as he promotes his first title fight.
 In August, he claimed he would punt the three-year-old son of Ian Machado Garry after a viral video of the boy upset over not meeting another UFC star.
 In September, Hokit angered fans with a series of "jokes" about the Sept. 11 tragedy. 
 "Who's the fastest readers in the world? 9/11 victims, they could go through 110 stories in just a few seconds," Hokit said on Instagram. "I'm usually skeptical of doing 9/11 jokes, because they usually never land."
